title: Behind MB&SP 4.0 — how the new version of MB&SP was made
author: Miłosz
content:
On September 26, 2026, MB&SP 4.0 enters Early Access.

But before I show the new version to users, I want to go back in time a little and tell you how much work it took to create a project that is now ready for release.

MB&SP 4.0 did not come together in a few weeks. In fact, the idea of moving away from the existing solution and creating my own approach to the platform appeared back in 2024.

That was the first time I seriously started thinking about MB&SP no longer being built on an off-the-shelf solution, but becoming a project developed entirely my way. The problem was simple: I didn’t always have the time.

Work, school, other projects, and everyday responsibilities meant that development regularly took a back seat. And when I did find the time to build the next version, very often after a while I would conclude that the project simply wasn’t good enough. It wasn’t what I wanted it to be.

And then it would end up in the trash.

Seven attempts at one project

Before the current version of MB&SP 4.0 came to be, my working project went through a total of seven different concepts and redesigns.

Not all of them were complete, working versions. Some were attempts to find the right direction, and some got much further. Most often it ended with just conceptual work and an interface design. Some solutions looked good at first, but during the work it quickly turned out that they didn’t deliver what I expected from the platform.

In hindsight, though, it was precisely those discarded versions that were necessary.

Each successive attempt helped me answer the question of what I actually expect from MB&SP.

I didn’t want to simply create yet another online store.

I wanted to build my own platform that could evolve continuously, without the limitations of off-the-shelf engines — from the product catalog and order handling to the further features that will appear in the future.

From an idea to my own project

That is why MB&SP 4.0 is more than just another redesign.

It is my own solution and my own project, developed from the ground up with the specific needs of MB&SP in mind.

I won’t go into the details of the architecture or the technology here. This text isn’t meant to be technical documentation. I would rather show the other side of the project — the one you usually don’t see when a user simply opens a finished website.

The final interface may look simple.

Behind it, however, are many hours of design, testing, changing concepts, fixing bugs, and making decisions that remain completely invisible to the user.

Why only now?

The shortest answer is: because this time I wanted to do it right.

Over the past years I tried several times to carry my own version of MB&SP through to the end. Sometimes I lacked the time. Sometimes the project had to give way to other things. And sometimes I simply concluded that the result wasn’t good enough.

So MB&SP 4.0 came together a little differently.

Instead of delivering the next version at all costs, I developed individual elements only once the whole began to form a coherent project.

This isn’t the end yet

On September 26, MB&SP 4.0 will be released as Early Access.

That matters, because I don’t treat the launch as the moment when the project is finished.

Quite the opposite.

Early Access marks the start of the next stage — users and customers will be able to use the platform, and I will be able to observe what works well, what needs improvement, and in which direction MB&SP should develop next.

09/26/2026 — MB&SP 4.0 Early Access.

Miłosz
Mily Unlimited
